definition: Making everyday journeys, or parts of journeys, by physically active means — chiefly walking, wheeling and cycling — rather than by motor vehicle.
plain: Getting about by walking, wheeling or cycling instead of going by car.
source: Department for Transport — The second Cycling and Walking Investment Strategy (CWIS2), 2022

definition: Travelling at around walking pace using a wheelchair, mobility scooter, rollator or other wheeled mobility aid; used alongside 'walking' so that active-travel policy includes people who do not walk.
plain: Getting about using a wheelchair, mobility scooter or other wheeled aid, at about walking speed.
source: Term used in UK active-travel policy (Sustrans; Wheels for Wellbeing; DfT CWIS2)
note: Confirm preferred source wording; the term is widely used but has no single statutory definition.

definition: The executive agency of the Department for Transport that sets standards for, funds and inspects walking, wheeling and cycling schemes in England.
plain: The government body that pays for and checks walking, wheeling and cycling schemes in England.

definition: The Government's statutory strategy for cycling and walking in England, setting objectives and the funding available to meet them; required by section 21 of the Infrastructure Act 2015.
plain: The government's long-term plan for more walking and cycling in England, and the money to pay for it.

term: Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan
full_term: Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan
definition: A local authority's long-term plan identifying the cycling and walking routes and improvements needed in its area, prepared using Department for Transport technical guidance.
plain: A council's plan for which walking and cycling routes to build or improve over the next few years.
source: Department for Transport — Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plans: technical guidance and tools

full_term: Local Transport Note 1/20: Cycle Infrastructure Design
definition: The Department for Transport's national design guidance for cycle infrastructure in England, setting standards for cycle routes, junctions and cycle parking.
plain: The national guide to designing safe cycle lanes, junctions and bike parking.
source: Department for Transport — Cycle infrastructure design (LTN 1/20), 2020

definition: The UK-wide network of signed routes for walking, wheeling and cycling, cared for by Sustrans.
plain: A network of signed routes across the UK for walking, wheeling and cycling.

definition: The national cycle-training programme in England, based on the National Standard for Cycle Training, which teaches practical skills for riding on today's roads across three levels.
plain: Cycle training, often run through schools, that teaches people how to ride safely on roads.
source: The Bikeability Trust; Department for Transport National Standard for Cycle Training

definition: A pedal cycle with an electric motor that assists only while the rider pedals, with a maximum continuous rated power of 250 watts and assistance that stops at 15.5 mph; in Great Britain it may be ridden like a pedal cycle by anyone aged 14 or over.
plain: A bike with a small electric motor that helps you as you pedal. You must be 14 or over to ride one.
source: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycles Regulations 1983 (as amended); GOV.UK — Electric bike rules

definition: A cycle designed or modified so that disabled people can ride it, such as a tricycle, handcycle, recumbent, tandem or wheelchair-transporting cycle.
plain: A bike made or changed so that disabled people can ride it, like a trike or a bike you pedal with your hands.

definition: A cycle built to carry heavy loads or passengers, often in a front box or on a long rear rack, and often electrically assisted.
plain: A strong bike made for carrying shopping, goods or children.

definition: A fixed steel stand shaped like an upturned 'U', to which two cycles can be locked by the frame and a wheel; the commonest form of public cycle parking in the UK.
plain: A metal hoop fixed in the ground that you can lock a bike to. Each one holds two bikes.
source: Department for Transport — LTN 1/20, chapter 11 (cycle parking)

definition: Cycle parking inside a locked or staffed space, such as a cycle hub, compound or locker, where access is controlled, giving more protection from theft than open stands.
plain: A locked or staffed place to leave your bike, so it is safer from theft.
source: Department for Transport — LTN 1/20, chapter 11 (cycle parking)
note: Matches the 'Secure cycle parking' category in the Tees Valley cycle-parking dataset.

definition: Cycle stands with a roof or canopy that protects parked cycles from the weather; usually open to anyone.
plain: Bike stands with a roof over them to keep bikes dry.
source: Department for Transport — LTN 1/20, chapter 11 (cycle parking)
note: Matches the 'Public sheltered racks' category in the Tees Valley cycle-parking dataset.

definition: A salary-sacrifice arrangement under which an employer loans cycles and cyclists' safety equipment to employees free of income tax on the benefit, using the exemption in section 244 of the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003.
plain: A way to get a bike through your job and pay for it a bit at a time from your wages, saving tax.
source: Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003, s.244; DfT — Cycle to Work scheme implementation guidance

definition: The Highway Code principle, introduced in January 2022, that road users who can cause the greatest harm have the greatest responsibility to reduce the danger they pose to others, with pedestrians at the top, then cyclists, horse riders and motorcyclists.
plain: A Highway Code rule. People driving bigger, faster vehicles must take the most care, because they could cause the most harm.
source: The Highway Code, introduction, rules H1–H3

definition: A signal-controlled crossing that pedestrians and cyclists can use together; there is no flashing amber phase, and cyclists may ride across.
plain: A traffic-light crossing that people walking and people on bikes can both use.

definition: A second stop line at traffic lights, set ahead of the main stop line, creating a reserved area where cyclists can wait in front of motor traffic.
plain: A box painted at traffic lights where people on bikes can wait in front of cars.

definition: A path away from the carriageway that people walking, wheeling and cycling are all legally allowed to use, with or without a marked separation between them.
plain: A path that people walking and people on bikes are both allowed to use.

definition: A public right of way on which the public may walk, ride or lead a horse, and ride a pedal cycle, cyclists giving way to walkers and horse riders.
plain: A public path you can walk, cycle or ride a horse along. People on bikes must give way to walkers and horses.

definition: A section of kerb lowered to the level of the road so that people using wheelchairs, mobility scooters, pushchairs or cycles can cross without a step; at crossings it is usually paired with tactile paving.
plain: A place where the kerb is lowered to road level, so wheelchairs, buggies and bikes can cross easily.

definition: A change in the way people make journeys from one mode of transport to another — in transport policy, usually from the private car to walking, wheeling, cycling or public transport.
plain: When people change how they travel, for example leaving the car at home and cycling instead.
source: Standard transport-planning term; used in DfT's Cycling and Walking Investment Strategy

definition: A battery-powered vehicle for people with limited mobility; in law an 'invalid carriage', either Class 2 (for pavements, up to 4 mph) or Class 3 (may also be used on roads at up to 8 mph, and must be registered with the DVLA).
plain: A small electric vehicle for people who find walking hard. Some can only go on pavements. Bigger ones can also use roads.
source: Use of Invalid Carriages on Highways Regulations 1988; The Highway Code, rules 36–46

definition: A parking permit for disabled people, issued by local councils, that allows the holder to park closer to their destination, including in some places where others cannot.
plain: A permit that lets disabled people park closer to where they are going.
source: Chronically Sick and Disabled Persons Act 1970, s.21; GOV.UK — Apply for or renew a Blue Badge

definition: A wheelchair built to travel over sand, shingle and soft ground, typically with wide, low-pressure 'balloon' tyres and a sturdy, rust-resistant frame; most are pushed by a companion rather than self-propelled.
plain: A wheelchair with big, wide tyres that can roll over sand. Someone usually pushes it for you.
note: Generic description; check it matches the chairs the scheme lends (e.g. whether any are self-propelled or floating).

definition: A manual or powered wheelchair designed for rough or uneven ground such as grass, gravel, mud, beaches and countryside paths, using larger, wider or tracked wheels.
plain: A wheelchair made for rough ground, like grass, gravel, mud or sand.

definition: A manual wheelchair designed to be pushed by another person, with push handles and wheels too small for the user to propel it themselves.
plain: A wheelchair that another person pushes, because the wheels are too small to push yourself.

definition: An adult who provides or intends to provide care for another adult, other than under a contract or as voluntary work.
plain: Someone who looks after a family member or friend who needs help, without being paid for it.

definition: A larger accessible toilet with a height-adjustable changing bench, a ceiling hoist and room for up to two carers, for people who cannot use a standard accessible toilet; required in certain new large public buildings in England since 2021.
plain: A big accessible toilet with a hoist and a changing bench, for people who need more help than a normal accessible toilet gives.
source: Changing Places Consortium; Building Regulations Approved Document M (2021 amendment)

definition: A standard key that opens accessible toilets fitted with National Key Scheme locks across the UK, so disabled people can use them while they stay locked to others.
plain: A special key that opens locked accessible toilets around the UK.
source: Disability Rights UK — National Key Scheme

definition: Changes that service providers and employers must make, under the Equality Act 2010, to remove or reduce a substantial disadvantage that disabled people face — to how things are done, to physical features, or by providing extra aids.
plain: Changes that organisations must make so disabled people can use their services, like adding a ramp.

definition: A physical or mental impairment that has a substantial and long-term adverse effect on a person's ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities; 'long-term' means it has lasted, or is likely to last, at least 12 months.
plain: A health condition or impairment that makes everyday tasks a lot harder, and has lasted or will probably last a year or more.

definition: The charity that runs the lifeboat service around the coasts of the UK and Ireland and provides lifeguards on many beaches.
plain: The charity that runs lifeboats and beach lifeguards around the UK coast.

definition: The flags used by lifeguards on UK beaches: red-and-yellow flags mark the lifeguarded area for swimming and bodyboarding; black-and-white chequered flags mark the area for surfboards, kayaks and other craft; a red flag means it is dangerous to enter the water.
plain: Flags on the beach that show where it is safe to swim. Swim between the red and yellow flags. Never go in the sea when a red flag is flying.

definition: The predicted times of high and low water at a stretch of coast, which change daily; checking them shows when the beach will be covered by the sea.
plain: The times when the sea comes in (high tide) and goes out (low tide). They change every day.
source: UK Hydrographic Office — Admiralty EasyTide predictions

definition: A paved public walkway along a seafront, usually level and set above the beach.
plain: A wide, flat path that runs along the seafront.

definition: A roll-out mat laid across sand to create a firm surface for wheelchairs, pushchairs and people with limited mobility.
plain: A mat laid on the sand to make a firm path for wheelchairs and buggies.
note: Generic term; keep only if mats are (or will be) used at the scheme's beaches.

definition: A UK tax relief that lets charities and community amateur sports clubs claim an extra 25p for every £1 donated by a UK taxpayer, provided the donor makes a Gift Aid declaration.
plain: If you pay UK tax and say yes to Gift Aid, the charity gets an extra 25p from the government for every £1 you give.

definition: Someone who chooses to give their time, unpaid, to help an organisation, the community or other people.
plain: Someone who gives their time to help, without being paid.

definition: A cross-sector partnership of local organisations — community groups, businesses, public bodies and others — that works together to improve the local food system, from growing and cooking to access to food.
plain: A group of local organisations working together so everyone can get good food.

definition: A UK network of local food partnerships working to make healthy, sustainable food a defining feature of their area, with an award scheme for places.
plain: A national network that links food partnerships across the UK.

definition: Everything involved in feeding people — growing, processing, transporting, selling, cooking, eating and disposing of food — and the people, businesses and rules involved.
plain: Everything that gets food from the field to your plate, and what happens to what is left.

definition: Not having secure access, at all times, to enough safe and nutritious food because of a lack of money or other resources; measured in UK official statistics through the household food-security questions in the Family Resources Survey.
plain: Not being sure you can afford or get enough good food.
source: DWP — Family Resources Survey (household food security)

definition: A charitable service that gives emergency food parcels, free of charge, to people in crisis, usually on referral from a professional or agency that issues a voucher.
plain: A place that gives free emergency food to people in a crisis. You usually need a voucher from a support worker.

definition: A referral issued by a frontline professional — such as an advice worker, social worker or health visitor — that allows a person to collect food from a food bank.
plain: A note from a support worker that lets you get food from a food bank.

definition: A pre-packed bag or box of mainly non-perishable food, meant to provide nutritionally balanced meals for a set number of days.
plain: A bag of food from a food bank, with enough to make meals for a few days.

definition: A food bank that is not part of the Trussell network; many belong to the Independent Food Aid Network.
plain: A food bank run by a local group on its own, not as part of a big national network.

definition: The UK charity, formerly the Trussell Trust, that supports a national network of food banks and campaigns to end the need for them.
plain: A national charity that supports a big network of food banks.

definition: A UK network of independent food banks and other food-aid providers that campaigns for a cash-first approach to food insecurity.
plain: A network that links up local food banks that are not part of Trussell.

definition: An approach to food insecurity that puts getting money into people's hands — through benefits advice, grants or cash payments — first, so they can buy their own food, with food aid as a last resort.
plain: Helping people get enough money to buy their own food, so they do not need a food bank.

definition: A shop that sells food and household essentials at reduced prices, often using surplus stock, usually to members who live locally or meet set criteria, and often with wider support on offer.
plain: A shop selling food and basics at low prices, often for members.
note: The Food Power Together map lists community groceries under social supermarkets.

definition: A membership food club where members pay a small weekly fee in return for a choice of groceries worth considerably more.
plain: A food club. You pay a small amount each week and choose food worth a lot more.

definition: A low-cost community shop selling surplus food that would otherwise go to waste, for a small donation or fee, usually to anyone who signs up.
plain: A low-cost shop selling spare food that would otherwise be thrown away.
source: Food Power Together service directory (local usage)
note: Local term; definition drawn from the eco shops listed on the FPT map — confirm with partners.

definition: A shared fridge in a public or community space where surplus food from shops, businesses and households is shared free with anyone.
plain: A fridge in a community space where anyone can take or leave spare food for free.

definition: Good-to-eat food that would otherwise be wasted — for example through over-production, short dates or packaging errors — which can be redistributed to people through charities and community groups.
plain: Food that is still fine to eat but would be thrown away, so it is given away or sold cheaply instead.

definition: The UK charity network that redistributes surplus food from the food industry to charities and community groups.
plain: A charity that collects spare food from shops and factories and passes it to local groups.

definition: A free or low-cost cooked meal served in a community setting such as a church, community centre or café, often offering company and support as well as food.
plain: A free or cheap hot meal you can eat with other people at a community place.
note: Covers the 'Hot food' category on the FPT map.

definition: A shared piece of land, such as a community garden or allotment, where local people grow fruit, vegetables and flowers together.
plain: A shared garden where local people grow fruit and vegetables together.

definition: A Department for Education-funded programme, delivered by local councils, that offers free healthy meals and enriching activities in the school holidays to children who receive benefits-related free school meals.
plain: Free holiday clubs with healthy meals for children who get free school meals.
source: Department for Education — Holiday activities and food programme

definition: Food insecurity that children experience during the school holidays, when they do not receive free school meals.
plain: When children go hungry in the school holidays because there are no school dinners.

definition: Meals provided free at school to pupils from families who receive certain benefits, including Universal Credit, and to all infant pupils (Reception to Year 2) in state-funded schools in England.
plain: Free school dinners for children from families on some benefits, and for all children in Reception to Year 2.
source: GOV.UK — Apply for free school meals
note: Eligibility rules change; re-check against GOV.UK before agreeing.

definition: An NHS scheme that gives people who are at least 10 weeks pregnant, or have a child under four, and who receive certain benefits, a prepaid card to buy milk, fruit, vegetables, pulses and infant formula, plus free vitamins.
plain: A free NHS payment card for families on some benefits, to buy milk, fruit and vegetables for young children.

definition: Government funding given to local councils in England to help households most in need with the cost of essentials such as food, energy and water.
plain: Government money that councils use to help families in need pay for food, energy and water.
source: DWP — Household Support Fund guidance for local councils
note: Time-limited fund renewed year by year; confirm it is still running (or what replaced it) before agreeing.

definition: A non-profit, community-controlled body that owns and manages land or other assets for the long-term benefit of a local community.
plain: A local group that owns land or buildings and runs them for the good of the community.

definition: A group of residential streets where through motor traffic is stopped by filters such as bollards, planters or camera-enforced gates, while every address can still be reached by car.
plain: A set of streets where cars can still get to every home, but cannot cut through, so the streets are quieter for walking and cycling.
note: Abbreviation clashes with LTN 1/20 (Local Transport Note) — the id keeps them apart; consider whether to show the abbreviation at all.

definition: A road outside a school that is closed to motor traffic at drop-off and pick-up times, so children can walk, wheel, scoot or cycle to school more safely.
plain: A road by a school that is closed to cars when children arrive and leave.

definition: A lane marked on the carriageway for cycles. A mandatory lane, marked by a solid white line, must not be entered by other vehicles while it is in operation; an advisory lane, marked by a broken line, should not be entered unless it is unavoidable.
plain: Part of the road painted for bikes. Cars must not drive in it when it has a solid white line.

definition: A cycle route physically separated from motor traffic, and usually from people walking, by kerbs, islands or a change in level.
plain: A bike lane with a kerb or barrier between it and the cars.

definition: Textured paving that blind and partially sighted people can feel underfoot or with a cane, used to warn of crossings, platform edges and other hazards; different patterns carry different meanings.
plain: Bumpy paving at crossings and edges that people with sight loss can feel with their feet or a cane.
source: Department for Transport — Guidance on the use of tactile paving surfaces

definition: A scheme that lets people hire a cycle, often an e-bike, for short trips, collecting and returning it at docking stations or marked parking zones, usually through an app.
plain: A way to rent a bike for a short trip, often using a phone app.

definition: A route the public has a legal right to use, recorded on the local council's definitive map; the main types are footpaths, bridleways, restricted byways and byways open to all traffic.
plain: A path everyone has the right to use, shown on the council's official map.
source: Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, s.53 (definitive map and statement)

definition: A plan that each highway authority must publish and review, assessing how well its local rights of way meet the needs of walkers, cyclists, horse riders and people with mobility problems, and setting out improvements.
plain: A council's plan to make public paths better for walkers, cyclists, horse riders and disabled people.
source: Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000, s.60

definition: The legal term for the pavement alongside a road, set aside for people on foot; cycling on it is not allowed unless it is signed as shared use.
plain: The pavement next to a road. You must not cycle on it unless signs say bikes are allowed.

definition: A free or low-cost drop-in session where a mechanic checks cycles for safety and makes small repairs and adjustments on the spot.
plain: A free or cheap session where someone checks your bike is safe and fixes small problems.

definition: A toilet designed for disabled people, with more space, grab rails and an emergency alarm cord; many are locked with a National Key Scheme (RADAR) key.
plain: A bigger toilet with rails and an alarm cord, made for disabled people.

definition: Moving from one seat to another — for example from your own wheelchair into a beach wheelchair — with or without help from another person or equipment such as a transfer board or hoist.
plain: Moving from one seat to another, like from your wheelchair into a beach wheelchair.
note: Check what help volunteers can and cannot give with transfers before agreeing.

definition: A scheme in which people wear a sunflower lanyard, pin or badge to show discreetly that they have a non-visible disability and may need help, understanding or more time.
plain: A sunflower lanyard or badge that shows someone has a disability you cannot see, and may need help or more time.

definition: The idea that people are disabled by barriers in society — such as steps, attitudes or a lack of information — rather than by their impairment or condition.
plain: The idea that people are disabled by things like steps and attitudes, not by their bodies or minds.
source: Scope — the social model of disability

definition: A beach with features that make it easier for disabled people to reach and enjoy, such as step-free access, accessible toilets and parking, and equipment like beach wheelchairs.
plain: A beach that is easier for disabled people to get to and enjoy.

definition: A ramp running down from the promenade or shore towards the sea, originally for launching boats; often the step-free route onto a beach.
plain: A ramp down to the beach, first built for boats. It is often the way onto the sand with no steps.

definition: A strong current running out to sea from the shore, which can quickly carry people into deeper water.
plain: A strong flow of water that pulls out to sea and can sweep people away from the beach.

definition: The emergency service, part of the Maritime and Coastguard Agency, that coordinates search and rescue at sea and around the UK coast; in an emergency at the coast, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.
plain: The emergency service for the sea and coast. If someone is in trouble at the beach, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.

definition: Any equipment that helps a person move about, such as a walking stick, crutches, a walking frame, a rollator, a wheelchair or a mobility scooter.
plain: Something that helps you get about, like a walking stick, a frame or a wheelchair.

definition: A walking frame with three or four wheels, hand brakes and usually a seat for resting.
plain: A walking frame with wheels, brakes and often a seat.

definition: In England, a household is fuel poor if it lives in a home with an energy-efficiency rating of band D or below and, after paying for the energy it needs, would be left with an income below the poverty line (the Low Income Low Energy Efficiency measure).
plain: When a family cannot afford to heat their home properly, often because the home is hard to keep warm.
source: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero — Fuel poverty statistics

definition: A free, welcoming, heated public space — often in a library, church or community centre — where people can keep warm and find company in winter, sometimes with hot drinks or food.
plain: A free, warm place to go in winter, often with a hot drink and company.

definition: A review of a person's circumstances to find out which benefits, grants and discounts they could claim but may be missing.
plain: A check to find out if you could get money or help you are not claiming yet.

definition: A means-tested benefit for people over State Pension age on a low income; receiving it can also open the door to other help, such as with housing costs, council tax and heating.
plain: Extra money for older people on a low income. Getting it can help you get other support too.

definition: A reduction in council tax for people on a low income or claiming certain benefits, run by each local council under its own local scheme.
plain: A discount on your council tax if you are on a low income.
source: GOV.UK — Apply for Council Tax Reduction

definition: A score from 0 to 5 given by the local council after inspecting a food business, showing how well it meets food hygiene law; 5 means hygiene standards are very good.
plain: A score from 0 to 5 that shows how clean and safe a place that serves food is.
source: Food Standards Agency — Food Hygiene Rating Scheme

definition: Ingredients that can cause allergic reactions; food businesses, including charities and community groups that provide food, must tell people if their food contains any of the 14 major allergens set out in law.
plain: Foods some people react badly to, like nuts or milk. Places that give out food must say if their food contains them.
source: Food Standards Agency — Food allergy and intolerance

definition: Date labels on food. A use-by date is about safety: food must not be eaten, sold or given away after it. A best-before date is about quality: food can still be eaten, and redistributed, after it if it is in good condition.
plain: 'Use by' means do not eat it after that date. 'Best before' means it is still fine to eat after the date, but may not be as nice.
source: Food Standards Agency — Best before and use-by dates

definition: A group session where people learn to cook simple, low-cost, healthy meals, often eating together afterwards.
plain: A group where you learn to cook cheap, healthy meals, and often eat them together.

definition: A food-buying group run by its members, who pool their money to buy food in bulk at wholesale prices and share it out.
plain: A group of people who club together to buy food in bulk, so it costs less.
